title: Think Faster, Talk Smarter: How to Speak Successfully When You're Put on the Spot
description: Communicate like a pro when you're on the spot— at team meetings, job interviews, sales calls, social events, networking meetups, and more. Now revised and updated with insights on presence in the age of AI. “A road map to mastering the art of thinking quickly and speaking confidently, this is the perfect book for…anyone else who talks.” —Charles Duhigg, bestselling author of The Power of Habit , Smarter Faster Better and Supercommunicators Formal presentations can be stressful. But there’s another, much more common type of communication that is even harder to manage: spontaneous situations in which people ask us unexpectedly to stand up and contribute our thoughts—without a script. In these moments, we don’t always know what to say. All too often, we freeze up or stammer out a cringeworthy response and walk away wishing for a do-over. Sure, some people naturally have the gift of gab, but how can the rest of us learn to be calmer and more eloquent in the moment? Stanford lecturer, award-winning podcast host, and communication expert Matt Abrahams provides powerful, life-changing strategies for conveying your ideas on the fly. Think Faster, Talk Smarter explores how to connect with any audience, respond to the mood of the room, structure your thoughts for maximum impact, make your content concise and memorable, and more. Abrahams also shares best practices for everyday speaking, including delivering killer pitches, providing helpful feedback, making small talk, and fixing mistakes, as well as practical skills that make social interactions feel effortless. With a new chapter on AI and tactics for using it as an accelerator rather than a crutch, Abrahams reveals how to project a distinctly human presence that builds trust and sets you apart in critical conversations. description: Do you ever freeze up in conversations, wishing you knew exactly what to say? We’ve all been there—standing in a room full of people, desperately wanting to connect, but instead feeling awkward, overlooked, or unsure of how to keep the conversation flowing. title: Small Talk: 10 ADHD Lies and How to Stop Believing Them
description: The beloved authors of Dirty Laundry break down the harmful stereotypes about people with ADHD to help you stop being your worst fear-leader, start bigging yourself up, and live your best neurodivergent life. When “ADHD wife” Roxanne Pink and neurotypical husband Richard Pink asked their community of 2.5 million what the biggest ADHD struggle is, the thousands of replies changed everything. As they learned, the real enemy isn’t productivity or focus, but the toxic ADHD core beliefs we’ve internalized. With candor and kindness, they share personal stories to highlight and reframe the 10 big lies that ADHD people believe about themselves. From “I am lazy” to “Everybody hates me” and “I quit everything I start,” Small Talk will empower ADHDers and those who love them to navigate life with compassion, humor, and hope. Whether you were diagnosed early or are new to the neurospicy community, Small Talk will change your relationship with yourself and others. title: The Small Talk and Conversation Skills Handbook: A Daily Practice Plan for Easy Openers, R
description: The question arrives at the kitchen counter, drink in hand. "So what do you do?" And the brain goes flat. Not blank; flat . There are words in there and none of them will come forward . So the answer comes out four words long, the other person has nowhere to go with it, and the whole thing is over. Then comes the drive home, and the replay, and the one better sentence that shows up three hours too late. Most books on this hand over a list of clever lines and icebreaker questions for strangers. Lines are not the problem. The problem is that nothing has been rehearsed , so the body gets there before the sentences do, and the body has never read a tip list. Sean Ashford writes a shy introvert guide that treats conversation the way it actually works: a small set of repeatable moves , drilled in the places life already puts a person, until they run without being asked . Not communication charisma. Not scripts for a business ballroom. Practice. And the rooms in this book are real rooms. School gates, gyms, waiting rooms, the office kettle, the counter where somebody is looking for a parcel. Hundreds of those a year, against maybe one professional networking function with a name badge. In The Small Talk and Conversation Skills Handbook, you will discover: The four moves that hold every conversation together, and why learning them in order matters more than learning more of them The three questions to ask about a room before opening a mouth, so a good line never lands on someone who was never available to hear it Why the Open is only ten words and about four seconds long, and the three ways in that cover almost every situation worth entering The second sentence , not hello, is where conversations die; the moves for overcoming awkwardness and keeping the floor from disappearing
